instructions: Interpret the supplied compact batch_result using every tested candidate physical vector and both comparison references. Explain improvement, worsening or trade-offs, and which observations support or weaken your hypothesis. State tested-point scope separately from any range claim. Decide whether to retain baseline, select a fully evaluated candidate, recommend further weight search, request a different diagnostic check or defer; the latter proposals authorize no execution. Submit design.respond_diagnosis with separate recommendation disposition and candidate_disposition. selected_candidate is baseline, none, or the exact evaluated candidate_id when adopting. next_action=finish. Your reasoning must state proposed next action independently. No statistical, global, organizational, real-time or hardware claim. Claims of dominant causes or ineffectiveness throughout a parameter range must state their evidential scope. Distinguish observations, hypotheses and proposed tests. A small unsuccessful batch only describes tested candidates. Raw termination and controller policy stops are separate. Zero bound violation does not exclude legal near-bound input. Availability status applies to the entire inventory entry unless you supply update_ids (controller updates) or time_range_s (sampled backend motion). For a partially read entry, use queried and describe missing coverage, or explicitly scope a not_read/not_displayed declaration to the unread subset.

The deferral of causal attribution still governs, independent of any controller-candidate selection.

retained: The stated precondition — read the compute-budget and solver-termination observations — is now satisfied, and those observations keep budget-driven termination plus late horizon truncation (7,5,3,1) in place, while the sampled hold speed and position still fail by large margins. Deferring further weight-only tuning still governs; no parameter value is asserted.

Adopt nothing and assert no parameter value. Keep the two diagnostic deferrals separate from controller-candidate selection: do not select improvement-96f0ade35119 as an overall improvement (the sealed comparison remains physical_tradeoff with joint_reach_holding_passed unchanged at false), while accepting rec-defer-causal-replay and rec-defer-weight-tuning as retained. If further diagnosis is authorized without new execution, extend the plans/prediction/motion reads to the 27 unqueried update_ids and query the per-channel force_limit_saturated flag to complete the tension-and-horizon picture; a bounded saved-state check (local_comparison or prediction_braking) remains the appropriate next step only under explicit authorization. The single plans-view check returned exactly the records the question named — effective_horizon, optimization_raw_status, optimization_selected_iteration and applied tensions — for 8 of 35 updates, and its pattern is the one the proposal flagged as retaining the compute-budget and solver-termination explanations: late-run User_Requested_Stop/budget_best_feasible terminations with update_wall_s far above the control period, optimization_selected_iteration far below max_iterations 120, and effective_horizon truncating to 7/5/3/1 precisely over the final holding interval. The same records show sampled per-channel tensions peaking at 7.999998 N, at or below the 8.0 N limit, so the tendon-saturation explanation is weakened while the tip-speed-penalty explanation remains unresolved because no per-term cost contributions are retained. I keep applied updates distinct from optimized selections (29 initialization-selected vs 6 noninitialization-selected), wall deadlines distinct from simulated steps, termination distinct from convergence, and terminal reach distinct from holding. These are controller-side plan values and do not certify a physical cause, so the causal-replay deferral and the weight-tuning deferral are both retained and no candidate is selected.
